I'm writing this from a country with socialized health care.

They tax cigarettes because they figure that the tax money will go to offset any damage people do to themselves by smoking. The government also ran several anti-smoking campaigns, and have those gnarly pictures of cancerous lungs and hearts and stuff on tobacco products. It's also illegal for anyone under 19 to purchase tobacco products in my province. And if you DO go to purchase them, they're all hidden away behind a screen - you can't see the product, you have to know exactly what you want and ask for it. As a result, tobacco usage has been on a steady decline since the 80's (IIRC). I'm also pretty sure that they are not allowed to advertise tobacco products anywhere (TV, magazines, billboard, etc.)

Alcohol is similarly regulated in this province, though there aren't nasty pictures of rotting livers or anything on bottles of wine or whatever. You still have to be 19 to purchase alcohol, and up until recently, you could only buy it in government-run stores (this summer the government started allowing beer & wine to be sold in some grocery stores, but not all of them). And alcohol is taxed to high heaven - to buy a 26er (750mL) of Smirnoff vodka here, it's something like $25 CAD. Again, they figure the extra taxes on the alcohol will help offset the healthcare costs associated with people who use alcohol.

I don't know if it will work, but I think the government needs to start taxing junk food. They should stop their sugar and corn subsidies, and start advertising fruits, vegetables, and other healthy foods. I think these advertisements need to be aimed towards kids.
